evidence: pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go:41-49 reads the cache under RLock, releases it, and then takes the write Lock at :48 without checking the cache again. In non-Dev mode, N goroutines that hit a cold cache at the same time each wait for the write lock in turn, and each one re-reads and re-parses build/assets-manifest.json (:60), a file of roughly 1500 entries. Re-checking `cfg.Env != setting.Dev && entryPointAssetsCache != nil` after Lock() is the standard double-checked pattern and removes that repeated IO. This is only a performance issue: the result is still correct, since every rebuild produces the same data and all writes happen under the lock. It only happens on a cold cache (first requests after startup) and never in Dev mode, where rebuilding every time is intended. The fix is small, so it is worth doing but not required.

This is a generic docstring-coverage check, not a finding about this change. The PR's real change is limited to pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go:35-49: it adds a mutex and wraps the cache in RLock/Lock. GetWebAssets (:40) had no doc comment in the base commit (3ce1a5b0 webassets.go:36) either. The PR adds no new exported API, and the package has no convention that requires doc comments. Grafana's Go lint setup enforces no 80% docstring threshold. The new mutex already has an explanatory comment (:36 'guard entryPointAssetsCache').
